symptom: Tap Add to cart on the same product several times, fast. The header badge settles on the wrong number. Refresh and open the cart: instead of one line with the right quantity, there are several separate lines of quantity 1. On the Dumbbell Set (stock 3), tapping 5 times fast can put more units in the cart than the shop has in stock.
description:
A small but realistic shop (React + a simulated Express-style backend) with login, a catalog, a cart and checkout. **The cart is broken.** Your job is to find out why and fix it, in every layer where the problem lives.

## 1. Run it

Click **Run** to start the preview, then log in with `asha@example.com` or `ravi@example.com`, password `password123`.

The Terminal tab is your shell for this question -- type `help` there to see every command. The Network tab's Timeline view lists responses in the order they actually arrived (the `#N` label is send order, so out-of-order arrivals are easy to spot), and the Logs tab's Server filter shows the server reading, pricing and writing the cart as each request is handled -- both built into this platform, for every question.

This question also ships the reference lab's own `?debug=1` Request-log panel. It only works in a real browser tab -- open **Open in new tab** first, then add `?debug=1` to that tab's URL (there's no address bar in the embedded preview to type a query string into). It shows every "add to cart" response in the order it *arrived*, next to what the cart badge currently shows -- `?debug=0` turns it off again.

## 2. What is broken

Support is getting tickets like this one:

> "I tapped **Add to cart** on the Yoga Mat three times quickly. The cart number in the header said 3, then 2, then 1. I refreshed and now there are **three separate Yoga Mat lines** in my cart. Someone else says they ended up with more Dumbbells in their cart than the shop even has."

There is no error in the console and every request returns HTTP 200. There are **three distinct problems**. They look like one bug, but each one lives in a different layer and has a different fix.

### Problem 1: The cart badge shows the wrong number

| Right after the taps | A few seconds later |
|---|---|
| ![Two responses have arrived; the badge shows 2](/questions/flipkart-cart-lab/img/01-mid-flight.png) | ![All responses have arrived; the badge shows 1](/questions/flipkart-cart-lab/img/02-badge-wrong.png) |

These two screenshots (and the three more later in this page) are from the real reference lab this question is ported from -- same bug, same shape, but a different catalog. (The dark panel in the screenshots is the `?debug=1` Request-log panel described in section 1 -- it exists here too, just via "Open in new tab".) Treat the screenshots as "this is what the bug looks like," not a pixel-accurate preview of this platform's UI.

**Tapping Add to cart on the Yoga Mat by hand will not reproduce this bug here.** In this simulation, responses reach the client in the order the server actually finishes them, so a hand-tapped burst correctly settles on the true total (3) -- the opposite of what the screenshots show. (The real reference lab delays the *response*; this simulation's timing lives before the write instead, which is why hand-tapping behaves differently here. Not something you need to fix.)

For an exact, repeatable look at the actual bug, use the Terminal tab:

```
npm run repro -- stale
```

(log in first and stay on the catalog page). It drives the real Add to cart button three times itself and hands the three responses back out of order -- the way a slow, congested network can -- then prints the badge's value after each one lands. On the untouched code it ends with `BUG: the badge settled on 1, but the server holds 3 -- an older response overwrote a newer one`.

**Expected:** the badge always settles on the true cart total, whatever order the responses arrive in -- `npm run repro -- stale` should end with `OK`, not `BUG`.

### Problem 2: The cart has duplicate lines

Click **Cart** in the header to open it -- **don't refresh the browser**: a real refresh restarts the simulated store and logs you out, wiping out the very taps you're trying to look at.

![Cart page with three separate Yoga Mat lines, each of quantity 1](/questions/flipkart-cart-lab/img/03-cart-after-refresh.png)

You tapped on one product, so there should be **one** Yoga Mat line with quantity **3**. Instead the cart contains **three** lines of quantity 1. The simulated store shows the same thing (`npm run db:inspect`).

**Expected:** one line per product per cart, with the right quantity, in the UI **and** in the simulated store. Fixing only the UI is not enough: the stored data itself is wrong.

### Problem 3: The cart can hold more than is in stock (overselling)

The **Dumbbell Set** has only **3** in stock (the catalog says "Only 3 left"). Tap **Add to cart** on it **exactly 5 times as fast as you can**, then click **Cart** in the header to look at it (not a browser refresh -- same reason as Problem 2):

| Catalog | Cart | Checkout |
|---|---|---|
| ![Catalog showing Only 3 left on the Dumbbell Set](/questions/flipkart-cart-lab/img/04-catalog-only-3-left.png) | ![Cart holding 5 Dumbbell Sets](/questions/flipkart-cart-lab/img/05-oversold-cart.png) | ![Checkout fails with an out-of-stock message](/questions/flipkart-cart-lab/img/06-checkout.png) |

The cart now holds **5** dumbbells for a product with a stock of 3, and checkout fails with "An item in your cart just went out of stock", a nasty surprise for the customer.

**Expected:** at most 3 taps succeed. The rest must be rejected with HTTP `409 OUT_OF_STOCK` (the UI already knows how to show that message).

### Good to know (these are not extra bugs)

- **+, minus and Remove act on the whole product.** They replace or delete *every* line of that product, not only the one you clicked. With the duplicate lines from Problem 2, pressing **+** on one line collapses all three lines into a single line, and the badge drops. That is a knock-on effect of Problem 2: once there is one line per product these buttons behave as you would expect, so you do not need to change them.
- **A route that throws gets answered, it does not crash the server.** If something rejects a duplicate row (for example after you add a uniqueness guard), the simulated backend replies `500 INTERNAL` and keeps running -- you'll see it in the Logs tab. The page shows "Something went wrong. Please try again." A message there is a clue, not a new bug.

## 3. Reproduce without clicking

Tapping fast enough to trigger Problems 2 and 3 by hand depends on your speed. To get the same result every time, use the Terminal tab:

```
npm run repro -- stale   # problem 1 -- log in first, stay on the catalog page
npm run repro -- dup     # problem 2
npm run repro -- stock   # problem 3
npm run db:inspect       # look at what's actually stored
```

Each one sends a quick burst of real "add to cart" requests (60ms apart, through the same network path the app itself uses -- watch them land in the Network tab) and prints, for each response, the order it arrived in and what ended up in the simulated store. The rows each scenario creates are left there on purpose: run `npm run db:inspect` right after to look at them. Press **Run** to start over from a fresh store.

### Why it is deterministic

The lab simulates a slow internal pricing service with **fixed**, not random, delays: the 1st, 2nd and 3rd request of a burst wait 800ms, 450ms and 100ms respectively, so responses come back in reverse order every time. That is why `npm run repro` always reproduces the same result, and why rapid hand-tapping doesn't.

## 4. Your goal

Make rapid taps behave correctly end to end:

- [ ] The badge and the cart page always match the server, whatever order responses arrive in (problem 1)
- [ ] There is exactly one cart line per product, in the UI and in the simulated store (problem 2)
- [ ] The cart can never hold more units of a product than its stock (problem 3)
- [ ] `npm test` passes (12 tests)
- [ ] `npm run repro -- stale`, `-- dup` and `-- stock` all print clean results

Rules of the game: don't weaken the tests, and don't hide the symptom (for example by debouncing the button), because a second tab or device would still break it.

Stuck? Use the **Hints** button below -- hints are revealed one at a time, roughly in the order these problems appear.

## 5. Tests

Run `npm test` in the Terminal tab -- fast, unscored, and it re-bundles your current edits even if you haven't pressed Run. On the untouched code, 6 of 12 tests fail:

| Failing test | Problem |
|---|---|
| client: `does not let a stale response overwrite a newer cart` | 1 |
| `three rapid adds of the same product give ONE line with quantity 3` | 2 |
| `rapid adds on top of an existing line do not lose increments` | 2 |
| `the database itself rejects duplicate (cart, product) lines` | 2 |
| `concurrent adds can never oversell the available stock` | 3 |
| `checkout charges exactly what the cart shows and decrements stock` | knock-on effect of 2 and 3 |

The other tests already pass. They guard behaviour that must keep working while you fix things -- for example, an unexpected error inside add-to-cart gives a 500 and the server keeps running.

**Submit** runs this same suite for real, server-side, and that real pass/fail is what's graded -- not an AI's read of your diff.

## What's in the simulated store

No real database here -- `server-sim/db.js` holds everything in memory, reset fresh every time you press **Run**.

| Table | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `products` | 7 products. `pricePaise` is the price in paise. `stock` is units available |
| `carts` | One cart per user. `version` goes up by one on every change to that cart |
| `cartItems` | The lines in a cart: `cartId`, `productId`, `quantity` |
| `orders` | Placed orders -- a snapshot of what was bought and at what price |

Products with interesting stock levels for this question: **Yoga Mat** (id 43, stock 5) and **Dumbbell Set** (id 49, stock 3). Demo users: `asha@example.com` and `ravi@example.com`, password `password123`.

Look inside with `npm run db:inspect` in the Terminal tab any time -- it prints the cart lines, which ones are duplicates, and the carts.
hints: Log in, stay on the catalog, and type `npm run repro -- stale` in the Terminal tab. It taps Add to cart on the Yoga Mat three times and lets the responses come back newest-first, the way a slow network can. It prints the order the responses ARRIVED in and every number the header badge showed. Does the badge end on the cart's real total, or on whichever response happened to arrive last?
That's Problem 1, in src/context/CartContext.jsx. Its mutate() function calls setCart() for whatever response arrives, with no way to tell a late (stale) response apart from the newest one.

Refresh the page after a burst of taps and open the cart. Problem 2 lives where the cart is actually stored: server-sim/cartHandlers.js reads what the cart currently holds, then awaits a network-like delay, then writes — and nothing stops two requests from both reading before either writes.

Fixing cartHandlers.js alone isn't the whole fix for Problem 2 — one of the tests inserts directly into the simulated database, bypassing your route entirely. Check server-sim/db.js: does anything stop two rows for the same (cart, product) pair from existing side by side?

Problem 3 (the Dumbbell Set oversold) and Problem 2 share a root cause — the same stale read in cartHandlers.js that lets duplicate rows through also lets the stock check pass more times than it should.
